adults.title: He Has Your Exact Location
adults.big_idea: The Lord knows exactly where we are, loves us completely, and stays at our side as He guides us toward the righteous desires of our hearts.
adults.objective: Learners will describe how the Savior loves first and then guides, and will choose one small practice this week that helps them notice Him at their side.
prepare: Read Sister Muñoz Spannaus's talk, noticing that she speaks to the young women of the Church. This lesson asks what the rest of us can learn as we listen in.
Write her seven ways on the board or on one sheet of paper before class (see the last segment).
Bring paper and pens for silent writing.

segments.name: When the directions do not fit
steps: After the prayer, explain that Sister Muñoz Spannaus spoke to young women, and that today the class will listen for what her message teaches all of us about the Lord.

Retell her story briefly: driving to the dentist on the freeway, her phone thought she was on a parallel street and kept telling her to turn right where there was no place to turn. She pulled off and called her husband. Once she gave him her exact location, he could guide her where she wanted to go.
Ask the question below and take two or three short answers.
questions: When has the advice or direction you were getting not matched where you really were in life? What did you need instead?

segments.name: What the Lord knows
steps: Read aloud slowly the paragraph of the talk that begins with the key quote about our exact location. Ask learners to listen for each thing the Lord knows.
Give one minute of silence. Invite learners to write the one sentence from that paragraph they most need to believe today.
Have learners turn to a neighbor and share which sentence they chose and, if they wish, why.
Read the last two sentences again: He knows everything, and knowing everything about us does not make Him love us less.
questions: Why is it sometimes hard to believe that being fully known and being fully loved can go together?

segments.name: Loved first, then taught
steps: Divide into groups of three or four. Ask each group to read Mark 10:17–21 and find what the Savior did before He told the young man what he lacked.
Bring the groups back. Share the speaker's observation: the Savior's look conveyed only love, and only after transmitting that love did He tell the young man what he could do to improve.
Discuss the questions below. Let learners carry the conversation; add little.
Read President Oaks's words from this conference (aligned quote) as a second witness of how the Lord feels about each person.
questions: How does it change the way you hear correction from the Lord when you picture Him looking at you with love first?
The speaker taught that part of His love is giving us many opportunities and being patient as we learn. Where have you seen that patience in your own life?
What could it look like for us to love first when a child, a friend or someone we minister to needs guidance?

segments.name: At your side on the dark day
steps: Retell the speaker's experience faithfully: she had recently moved from Argentina to the United States and was learning English. Her calling involved teaching. One day she felt everything she said had been wrong. She felt as if she were in a black cloud, went to sleep in tears, and woke feeling the same. Then her husband gave her a priesthood blessing, and she felt the heavens open.
Read the words she received in that blessing from the key quotes, then her testimony that the Lord has greater power than the enemy.
Ask half the class to read Isaiah 41:13 and the other half Ether 12:27 silently, looking for what the Lord promises to do. Invite one comment from each half.
Invite one or two learners to answer the question below. Allow quiet; do not rush to fill it.
questions: When have you learned for yourself that the Lord was at your side, even though the hard thing did not go away at once?

segments.name: One small practice
steps: Point to the seven ways the speaker offered young women: partake of the sacrament humbly and begin each day asking for the companionship of the Holy Ghost; repent daily; study the scriptures to know God's character; study what it means to have ministering angels help you; protect your sleep; limit cell phone use; seek friends who are striving to follow the Lord.

Explain that she invited young women to listen to the Spirit and choose one to focus on. Suggest that adults can try the same pattern for themselves, and can encourage a young person they love who is working on hers.
Give two minutes of silent writing: Which one would most help me notice the Lord at my side? What is the first small step?
Close with your testimony that the Father, Jesus Christ and the Holy Ghost are at our side. Tell the class you will begin next week by asking what they noticed as they tried their one practice.

key_quotes.text: the Lord knows where you are; He has your exact location and can guide you.
He knows everything. And knowing everything about you does not make Him love you less.
Only after transmitting that love did He tell him what he could do to improve.
But the Father, Jesus Christ, and the Holy Ghost are at your side.

scriptures.use: Read in small groups. Find what the Savior did before He told the young man what he lacked, and talk about why the order matters.
Half the class reads it silently after the story of the priesthood blessing, looking for what the Lord promises to do with our hand.
The other half reads it silently, looking for what the Lord does with weakness. Connect it to the speaker's teaching that He knows how to turn weaknesses into strengths.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Oaks
aligned_quotes.text: He is relentless in His loving pursuit of each of you.

takeaways: The Lord knows exactly where I am, and knowing everything about me does not make Him love me less.
The Savior loves first and then shows us how to improve.
The Father, Jesus Christ and the Holy Ghost are at my side, and the Lord has greater power than the enemy.
act: Choose one of the seven ways and practice it for the next few weeks. Write down what you notice.
Begin each morning prayer this week by telling Heavenly Father honestly where you are and asking for the companionship of the Holy Ghost.
Before you correct or counsel someone this week, pause and let that person feel your love first.
Ask a young woman you know which of the seven ways she is working on, and encourage her.
adapt: At home with adults: skip the small groups. Read Mark 10:17–21 together, then let each person answer the question in the fourth segment.
Short on time: keep the second, third and fifth segments and tell the two stories in a sentence each.
Large class: do every discussion in pairs first, then take two comments from the whole room.

youth.title: Your List, His Directions
youth.big_idea: Heavenly Father knows exactly where you are and what you hope for, loves you perfectly, and will guide you toward the righteous desires of your heart.
youth.objective: Youth will begin their own list of good things they want in their lives and choose one of the speaker's seven ways to focus on for the next few weeks.
prepare: Read the talk. Sister Muñoz Spannaus speaks to young women; if young men are in your class, tell them plainly that they are listening in and that what she teaches about the Lord is true for them too.
Write each of the speaker's seven ways (from the sacrament through seeking good friends) on its own slip of paper, or be ready to send the talk link so youth can open it on their phones.
Bring paper and pens. Ask youth to have scriptures or the Gospel Library app ready.
Mark Articles of Faith 1:13, Mark 10:17–21 and Isaiah 48:17.

segments.name: Find your blue dot
steps: As soon as the prayer ends, ask everyone with a phone to open a map app and find the dot that shows where they are. Those without a phone look on with a neighbor.
Ask: What would happen to the directions if that dot were one street off?

Tell the speaker's story: on the freeway on her way to the dentist, her phone thought she was on a parallel street and kept telling her to turn right where there was no place to turn. She pulled off and called her husband. When she gave him her exact location, he guided her there.
Have one youth read the first key quote aloud. Then ask that phones go face down until they are needed again.

segments.name: Known and loved
steps: In pairs, read Mark 10:17–21. Challenge each pair to find what Jesus did before He answered the young man's question.
Share the speaker's point: the Savior's look conveyed only love, and only after that did He tell the young man how to improve.
Ask the first question below and give ten seconds of quiet before anyone answers. Then read the second key quote.
Ask the second question.
questions: If God knows everything about me, including what I am not proud of, how do I think He feels when He looks at me?
How would you pray differently if you really believed He looks at you the way He looked at that young man?

segments.name: Start your list
steps: Tell how the speaker, at about their age, left a lesson thinking about one line of the thirteenth article of faith. She spent that Sunday afternoon writing a list of good things she wanted in her life: things that would bring her closer to God and help her learn, contribute, create and be happy.
Read Articles of Faith 1:13 together. Ask youth to pick the one word in it that stands out to them and tell a neighbor why.
Read her invitation to study the thirteenth article of faith and create a list of aspirations (see invitations). Explain that she gave it to young women and that anyone in the room may take it up.
Give four minutes of silent writing. Each youth starts a list under four headings: learn, contribute, create, closer to God. No one will collect it.
Invite two volunteers to share one item each.

segments.name: Seven ways, pick one
steps: Form two or three teams. Give each team the seven slips, or have them open the talk to the seven ways. Allow one minute to read them.
Turn the slips over or close the phones. Teams have one minute to write all seven from memory. Check answers together; the team with the most wins bragging rights.

Ask each team to choose the one they think is hardest for people their age and explain why to the class. Expect sleep and phones to come up. Read the third key quote, on social media, and Elder Andersen's words (aligned quote).
Read President Oaks's invitation about friends, which the speaker gave as number seven (aligned quote).
Read her invitation to listen to the Spirit and choose one to focus on. Give thirty seconds of silence, then have each youth write the one they choose at the top of their list.
questions: Why do you think getting enough sleep and limiting phone use are on the same list as the sacrament and repentance?
What is the difference between feeling connected online and feeling heard face to face?

segments.name: When the black cloud comes
steps: Say honestly that making a list does not mean every day goes well. Tell the speaker's experience: newly moved from Argentina and still learning English, she taught in her calling and felt that everything she said had been wrong. She felt as if she were in a black cloud, went to sleep in tears, and woke up feeling the same.

Tell what happened next: her husband gave her a priesthood blessing, and she felt the heavens open. She was told that Satan wanted to destroy her self-esteem, and then that the Father, Jesus Christ and the Holy Ghost were at her side.
Have a youth read Isaiah 48:17 aloud and another read the fourth key quote.

Ask the question below. Accept one or two answers or let it rest in silence. If a youth describes feeling this way for a long time, speak with them afterward and encourage them to talk with a parent or leader.
questions: What helps you remember on a bad day that the Lord has not lost track of you?

segments.name: Lock it in
steps: Invite youth to pick up their phones once more and set a reminder or a lock-screen note naming the one way they chose.
Read the speaker's promise in her own invitation: we can look at our lives with the certainty that our Father in Heaven will guide us (see invitations).
Bear brief testimony that the Lord knows where each of them is. Tell them you will begin next week by asking who added to their list and how their one way is going.

key_quotes.text: the Lord knows where you are; He has your exact location and can guide you.
And knowing everything about you does not make Him love you less.

Social media makes us believe we are connected; however, it is a thief of our peace of mind, self-esteem, and the real connection that makes us feel loved, accepted, heard, and valued when spending time face to face with others.
I testify that the Lord has greater power than the enemy. He knows where you are and has promised to lead you by the hand.

scriptures.use: Read in pairs. Find what Jesus did before He told the young man what to do next.
Read together before the silent writing. Each youth picks one word that stands out and uses it to begin a list of good things to seek.
One youth reads it aloud after the black cloud story. Listen for what the Lord says He does for us.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Dallin H. Oaks
aligned_quotes.text: Seek friends … who are striving to follow the Lord … with whom you can feel the Spirit and … reinforce your faith.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Andersen
aligned_quotes.text: Our phone seems almost attached to our hand, bringing a flood of information, misinformation, and now artificial information.

invitations.text: I invite you to look at your life and what you want to achieve with enthusiasm and the certainty that your Father in Heaven will guide you on that journey
I invite you to listen to the Spirit to choose one to focus on over the next few weeks.
I invite you to study the thirteenth article of faith and to create your own list of aspirations.

takeaways: The Lord has my exact location, and knowing everything about me does not make Him love me less.
I can make a list of good things to seek and trust Heavenly Father to guide me toward them.
On the worst day, the Father, Jesus Christ and the Holy Ghost are at my side.
act: Finish your list this Sunday afternoon and keep it where you will see it.
Work on the one way you chose for the next few weeks, and tell a parent or leader which one it is.
Pick a bedtime and a place outside your bedroom to leave your phone for five nights this week.
Spend time face to face this week with a friend who helps you feel the Spirit.
adapt: Mixed class or a quorum: say at the start that the talk was given to young women. Young men can ask what the Lord would have them learn from it, and how they can support the young women they know.
At home or with two or three youth: skip the teams. Take turns reading the seven ways and let each person name the easiest and the hardest.
Short on time: do the first, third and fourth segments and send the black cloud story home as reading.

children.title: Jesus Knows Where I Am
children.big_idea: Heavenly Father and Jesus always know where I am, They love me, and They are at my side.
children.objective: Children will say that God is at their side and will draw one place where they can remember that He is with them.
prepare: Read the talk, especially the story of the phone directions and Mark 10:21.
Bring a flashlight, plain paper and crayons.
Cut or draw one paper circle to be a steering wheel.
Set a row of chairs along one side of the room and clear the floor so children can walk safely.

segments.name: Sing and pray
steps: Greet each child by name as they sit down.
Sing one verse of a song from the music list and invite a child to pray.
Teach today's truth with actions: point up for God, then pat the space beside you while saying “God is at my side.” Say it together three times.

segments.name: I know where you are
steps: Tell the children that when you say go, they walk quietly to any spot in the room and freeze.
When they freeze, name where each child is: by the door, next to the window, behind the chair. Play three rounds.
Gather the children and say that you could tell where they were because you could see them. Heavenly Father and Jesus always know where each of us is, in every place and at every time.
Ask the question below, then say the truth with actions again.
questions: Where are some places you go where Heavenly Father knows right where you are?

segments.name: The wrong turn
steps: Tell the children that Sister Muñoz Spannaus, a leader of the young women of the Church, told this story. Choose a driver to hold the paper steering wheel, a child to be the phone, and a helper who stands across the room.

The driver walks slowly beside the row of chairs. The phone keeps saying to turn right. Let the children see that the driver cannot turn; the chairs are in the way. The phone did not know where she really was.
The driver stops and calls the helper. Whisper the words for the driver to say: I am by the chairs near the door. Now the helper knows where she is and tells her how to walk to him.
Sit down and explain that Sister Muñoz Spannaus taught that the Lord always knows our exact location and can guide us. He never gets it wrong.
questions: Why could the helper guide her when the phone could not?

segments.name: Jesus looked and loved
steps: Tell the story from Mark 10 in simple words: a young man came running to Jesus and knelt down. He asked what he could do to gain eternal life. Before Jesus answered, He looked at the young man and loved him.
Let the children act it out once: run in place, kneel, look up.

Hold the flashlight low and shine it on each child's hands in turn, never toward faces. As the light rests on each child say: Jesus knows you, and Jesus loves you, using the child's name. The class repeats it for each child.
Teach that Heavenly Father and Jesus know all about us and love us with a perfect love.
questions: How do you feel when someone who loves you looks at you and smiles?

segments.name: Led by the hand
steps: Put the children in pairs. One closes his or her eyes; the partner holds a hand and leads slowly across the room to a chair. Then they trade. Remind everyone to walk slowly and gently.
Read Isaiah 41:13 aloud from your scriptures, or ask an older child to read it. Ask the children to listen for whose hand the Lord holds.

Tell them that Sister Muñoz Spannaus once had a very sad day. She was learning a new language and felt she had said everything wrong. She received a priesthood blessing and learned that the Father, Jesus Christ and the Holy Ghost were at her side.
Say the truth with actions together.
questions: How did it feel to have someone hold your hand when you could not see?

segments.name: Draw it
steps: Give each child paper and crayons. Ask them to draw themselves in one place they go, such as a classroom, a playground or their bed at night.
Have them add a bright yellow light beside their picture to remind them that God is at their side there.
Help them write the words God is at my side across the top, or write it for them.
Walk around and ask each child to tell you about the picture.

segments.name: Share and choose
steps: Let two or three children hold up their pictures and tell where God is with them.
Invite the children to do one thing this week: when they feel alone or worried, say a prayer and remember that God is at their side.
Bear your testimony in two sentences that Heavenly Father and Jesus know and love each child in the room.
Tell the children you will ask next week when they remembered. Send the pictures home.

key_quotes.text: the Lord knows where you are; He has your exact location and can guide you.
The Father, Jesus Christ, and the Holy Ghost are at your side.

scriptures.use: Tell the story in your own words and have the children act it out. An older child can read the first part of the verse aloud to find what Jesus felt for the young man.
Read aloud after the hand-holding walk. Children listen for whose hand the Lord holds.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Fale
aligned_quotes.text: I am a child of God and He loves me.

takeaways: Heavenly Father and Jesus always know where I am.
Jesus knows me and loves me.
act: When you feel alone or worried this week, say a prayer and remember that God is at your side.
Put your picture where you will see it when you wake up.
Teach the words and actions for God is at my side to someone at home.
music: If the Savior Stood Beside Me
I Am a Child of God

adapt.younger: For ages 3–7: shorten the wrong-turn story by playing the phone yourself and choosing only a driver. Lead each child by the hand yourself instead of pairing them. Repeat the truth with actions after every activity, and let the children draw freely while you write the words.
adapt.older: For ages 8–11: have them read Mark 10:21 and Isaiah 41:13 aloud and lead the freeze game. After the flashlight activity, read Elder Fale's words and ask: Jesus loved the young man before telling him how to do better. What does that teach you about how Jesus feels about you when you make a mistake?
